o: Count permutations of up to 14 distinct numbers where every consecutive pair divides one another. Brute force over 14! permutations is hopeless (~87 billion), but n <= 14 screams subset DP: 2^14 = 16384 masks. Define dp[mask][last] = number of ways to arrange the elements in 'mask' ending with element 'last' such that all adjacent constraints hold. Transitions append a new element compatible with 'last'. Example [2,3,6]: valid orders are [3,6,2] (3|6, 2|6) and [2,6,3] (2|6, 6%3==0), giving 2.
k: n <= 14 signals bitmask DP over subsets: 2^n * n states.
Compatibility of a pair depends only on the two values, so precompute an n x n boolean matrix.
Answer = sum of dp[full_mask][last] over all last.

a.i: Build dp over increasing mask popcount. For each (mask, last) with nonzero count, extend to any unused index nxt compatible with last. Because compatibility is a pairwise relation, the DP correctly counts all valid orderings without revisiting structure inside the mask.
s: Base case dp[1<<i][i] = 1 for every i.
Iterate masks ascending; for each (mask,last), add dp[mask][last] to dp[mask | 1<<nxt][nxt] for compatible unused nxt.
Return the sum of dp[(1<<n)-1][*] modulo 1e9+7.
a.t: O(2^n * n^2) — each of the 2^n * n states tries n extensions.
a.sp: O(2^n * n) for the DP table.

a.i: The same recurrence written as memoized dfs(mask, last): the number of valid completions given the used set and the last placed element. Top-down often visits far fewer states in practice because unreachable (mask, last) combinations are never computed.
s: Memoize dfs(mask, last) with base case mask == full returning 1.
Try every unused nxt with ok[last][nxt], summing dfs(mask | 1<<nxt, nxt).
Seed with dfs(1<<i, i) for each starting i and sum the results.
a.t: O(2^n * n^2) worst case — same state space, often faster in practice due to lazy evaluation.
a.sp: O(2^n * n) for memoization plus recursion stack O(n).

w: Bitmask DP is the intended solution whenever n <= ~20 and the objective depends on which items are used plus local ordering info. Pitfalls: modding inside loops (not just at the end), and remembering the answer sums over all possible last elements. Follow-ups: count permutations under a general pairwise predicate (same DP applies), or reconstruct one special permutation (store parent pointers).
